integrations.title: Integrations
integrations.description: Connect Naruvi to AI models, your mailbox, calendar and other tools.

ai.title: AI models
ai.description: AI features send relevant job text, verified profile facts, and available company research to the provider you choose.

mail.title: Mail and reminders
mail.description: Replies linked to your applications, next steps in your calendar, and a nudge on your phone.

people.title: Reaching people
people.description: Find a recruiter’s work email from their name and company.

research.title: Companies and pay
research.description: Public facts on company pages, and what similar roles pay on job pages.

connect.title: Job discovery, extension, API and export
connect.description: Find new postings, save jobs from your browser, let an AI assistant or your scripts use Naruvi, or take your data elsewhere.

export.title: Spreadsheets & export
export.description: Share your search with a coach or an employment agency, or keep your own records. Opens in Excel, Google Sheets, Numbers and LibreOffice.
export.body: One row per application: company, role, stage, fit, date applied, next step, emails, tags and links. For everything (profile, documents, settings) use the full JSON export in Settings → Your data.

finder.title: Email finder
finder.description: Find a recruiter’s or manager’s work email from their name and their company’s website, one contact at a time, with “Find email” on the Contacts page. Uses Hunter.io with your own key (free plan available).
finder.replaceKey: Paste a new key to replace it
finder.privacy: Only the name and the company’s domain are sent, and only when you click Find email. Write to people about relevant roles and respect their privacy and local rules (such as GDPR).

reply.title: Reply address per application
reply.description: Emails you send from Naruvi ask for replies at an address that names the application, so every reply is linked for sure. It still arrives in your inbox.
reply.label: Reply addresses
reply.plusHint: Works with Gmail, Outlook, Fastmail, Proton and most providers that accept “you+anything@”. Nothing to set up.
reply.forward: Forward every address of that domain to {email}. With Cloudflare: Email → Email Routing → Routing rules → Catch-all → Send to {email}. Any provider with a catch-all forward works the same.
reply.savedOnBody: New emails sent from Naruvi use them.

calendar.newLinkBody: The old link stopped working. Update it in your calendar app.
calendar.title: Calendar
calendar.description: Your dated next steps and scheduled interviews in your calendar. Reminders are all-day events; interviews keep their selected time and duration.
calendar.apple: File → New Calendar Subscription, paste the link.
calendar.outlook: add a calendar from the internet / on the network, paste the link.
calendar.google: it fetches links from Google’s servers, which can’t reach Naruvi on your computer. Download the file and import it instead.
calendar.events: {count, plural, one {# next step with a date right now.} other {# next steps with a date right now.}} Anyone with the link can read your next steps; reset it if you shared it by mistake.
calendar.off: Turn it on to get a private link your calendar app can subscribe to.

market.factsBody: Fill company pages with size, founding year, headquarters and industry from Wikidata and the French business registry (Annuaire des entreprises). Free, no account. Only the company’s name and website are sent.
market.salaryBody: Compare a job’s pay with what similar roles pay in the same city, using Adzuna’s market data (free key from developer.adzuna.com). Without it, jobs are still compared with the ones you saved, and link to Levels.fyi and Glassdoor.
market.salaryPrivacy: Only the job title and city are sent, when you open a job. Results are kept for a week. Works for France, the UK, Germany, the US and 12 more countries.

oauth.explain: Naruvi runs on your computer, so the first time you register your own app with Google or Microsoft (about 10 minutes, guided). Your mail never passes through anyone else’s server.
oauth.setupBody: Register Naruvi as your own app, then paste its details here. The secret is stored encrypted.
oauth.keepSecret: Leave empty to keep the saved secret
oauth.tenantHint: Work or school (Microsoft 365) accounts only — personal Outlook.com, Hotmail and Live accounts don’t work. Use common, organizations or your organization’s tenant ID. For a personal mailbox, use IMAP/SMTP instead.

google.0: In Google Cloud, create a project and enable the Gmail API.
google.1: OAuth consent screen: External, add yourself as a test user (no review needed for personal use).
google.2: Credentials → Create credentials → OAuth client ID → Web application. Add the redirect URI below.
google.3: Paste the client ID and client secret here.

microsoft.0: In Microsoft Entra → App registrations → New registration. Accounts: “any organizational directory and personal Microsoft accounts”.
microsoft.1: Redirect URI: platform Web, the address below.
microsoft.2: Certificates & secrets → New client secret. API permissions: add IMAP.AccessAsUser.All and SMTP.Send (Office 365 Exchange Online), offline_access, email.
microsoft.3: Paste the application (client) ID and the secret value here.

notifications.onBody: A test notification is on its way.
notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.description: Get a push on your phone or desktop when a company replies, a next step is due, or new job leads arrive. Uses ntfy: free, open source, and you can run your own server.
notifications.step1: Install the ntfy app on your phone (or open ntfy in a browser).
notifications.step2: Subscribe to the topic below. Anyone who knows a topic on ntfy.sh can read it, so keep the random name.
notifications.topicPlaceholder: Created for you when you save
notifications.keepToken: Leave empty to keep the saved token
notifications.tokenHint: Only for protected topics or your own server
notifications.encrypted: Stored encrypted, like your other keys.

toggle.leads: New job leads from alert emails
toggle.hide: Hide company names and roles in notifications

extensionConnect.title: Connect the browser extension
extensionConnect.body: The Naruvi extension in this browser asked to connect to your Naruvi.
extensionConnect.can: It will be able to read job postings you send it, save jobs, leads and contacts, and show what needs doing today. It gets its own key, which you can revoke anytime under Integrations → API & browser extension.
extensionConnect.notYou: Didn't click Connect in the extension yourself? Cancel.
extensionConnect.doneBody: The extension picks this up on its own and closes this tab. You can also close it yourself.
extensionConnect.revokeHint: Its key is listed under Integrations → API & browser extension.

api.title: API & browser extension
api.description: Let the Save to Naruvi extension, an AI assistant (MCP) or your own scripts use Naruvi. Each key works until you revoke it.
api.once: It won’t be shown again. Naruvi only keeps a fingerprint of it.
api.namePlaceholder: What it’s for, e.g. Browser extension
api.name: Key name

ext.title: Set up the browser extension
ext.body: One click sends the posting you’re looking at (including LinkedIn and other pages behind a login) to Naruvi.
ext.step1: Unzip it. In Chrome, Edge or Brave open chrome://extensions, turn on Developer mode, click Load unpacked and pick the naruvi-extension folder.
ext.step2: Its settings open by themselves, already set to {origin}. Click Connect, then approve here. No key to copy.
ext.firefox: Firefox: open about:debugging → This Firefox → Load Temporary Add-on and pick the zip. Firefox removes it when it restarts.

mcp.title: Connect an AI assistant (MCP) or your scripts
mcp.body: Ask Claude or another MCP client “what needs my attention?” or “move Dashlane to interviewing”. It reads and updates Naruvi through your API key and asks before changing anything.
mcp.desktop: Claude Desktop and other clients (mcpServers in their config file):
mcp.scripts: Your own scripts: send Authorization: Bearer nrv_… to {origin}/api/v1 (see docs/API.md).

mail.worksBody: {count, plural, one {# message} other {# messages}} in the inbox · sending {sending, select, ok {works} other {not set up}}
mail.connectedBody: Naruvi checks it every 5 minutes. Syncing now…
mail.synced: Checked {checked} emails, {stored} linked to your applications
mail.title: Email
mail.connectedDescription: Replies from companies are linked to your applications. Only matching emails are kept; the rest of your inbox is never stored.
mail.resendInfo: Sending uses Resend. Replies go to application aliases on {domain} and sync about every five minutes while Naruvi runs.
mail.readsFrom: Reads the inbox from {date} on. Sending uses {smtp}.
mail.newLinked: {count, plural, one {# new email linked} other {# new emails linked}}
mail.noMatches: {count, plural, one {Checked # unlinked email; no new application matches} other {Checked # unlinked emails; no new application matches}}
mail.disconnectBody: {count, plural, one {Naruvi removes the saved credential and deletes the # linked email it stored. Nothing is deleted from your mailbox.} other {Naruvi removes the saved credential and deletes the # linked emails it stored. Nothing is deleted from your mailbox.}}
mail.description: Connect the mailbox you apply from. Naruvi links replies to your applications and suggests what to do; it never changes anything or sends mail without your click.
mail.worksWith: Works with Gmail, Outlook, iCloud, Yahoo, Fastmail, Proton (Bridge) or any IMAP mailbox. Servers are filled in from your address.
mail.keepPassword: Leave empty to keep the saved password

help.gmail: Turn on 2-Step Verification, then create an app password at myaccount.google.com/apppasswords and paste it here.
help.outlook: Use an app password (account.microsoft.com → Security → Advanced security options). Some work accounts block IMAP; ask your admin.
help.icloud: Create an app-specific password at appleid.apple.com → Sign-In and Security.
help.fastmail: Create an app password in Settings → Privacy & Security → Integrations.
help.yahoo: Generate an app password in Account security.
help.proton: Run Proton Mail Bridge on this computer and use the password it shows (not your Proton password).
help.other: Find the IMAP and SMTP server names in your provider’s help pages. Use an app password if your provider offers one.

mail.runKey: Run npm run settings:key, then restart Naruvi.
mail.encrypted: Encrypted on this computer. Only emails about your applications are kept.

resend.intro: Use a sender on a verified Resend domain and an address that receives mail in Resend. Naruvi adds a per-application plus tag to the receiving address for replies.
resend.switch: Connecting Resend switches your active mail provider and keeps your linked emails.
resend.keepKey: Leave blank to keep the saved key
resend.keyHint: Use a full access key for sending and receiving. Naruvi stores it encrypted.
resend.fullAccess: Resend asks for full access to the selected team because receiving email requires it.
resend.runKey: Run npm run settings:key and restart Naruvi to enable secure storage.

apify.title: Job discovery
apify.description: “Discover” on the Jobs page finds postings that match your profile and search goals, and puts the best in your job leads. Nothing is saved until you import one. Uses Apify with your own token (about $1 to $3 per 1,000 postings).
apify.replaceKey: Paste a new token to replace it
apify.privacy: Only your goals' roles and places are sent to Apify. Scraping job boards may break their terms of use, so use it for your own search only.
apify.daily: Also search once a day in the background
apify.planEmpty: No active search goal names a role yet, so there is nothing to search for.
apify.planHelp: Built from the roles and places of your active search goals.
apify.planEmptyLink: Add roles to a search goal

modelSettings.saved: Saved. Naruvi will use these settings on its next AI request.
modelSettings.loaded: {count, plural, one {# model loaded. Select a model or type its ID.} other {# models loaded. Select a model or type its ID.}}
modelSettings.requestFailed: Could not complete the request. Try again.
modelSettings.title: Language model
modelSettings.description: Powers the assistant, job analysis, CVs, and cover letters.

hint.local: Start the server and load a model before connecting. The server must be reachable from Naruvi.
hint.gateway: Use one account to access models from multiple providers.
hint.cloud: Use an API key from your provider account.
hint.custom: Connect any server that supports the OpenAI Chat Completions API.

modelSettings.regionHint: Choose the region for your Bedrock key. Pick a model that supports Chat Completions on Bedrock Mantle.
modelSettings.baseUrlHint: Enter the base URL, without the /chat/completions suffix.
modelSettings.keepKey: Leave blank to keep the current key
modelSettings.keyRemoved: The current key will be removed when you save.
modelSettings.keyOther: Your current key belongs to a different endpoint.
modelSettings.keyEnv: The key is currently set on the server. Saving moves it to encrypted storage.
modelSettings.noEncryption: To save an API key, set SETTINGS_ENCRYPTION_KEY to a random 64-character hex value on the server and restart Naruvi.
modelSettings.modelHint: Load your provider’s list or enter the ID manually. Choose a model with tool support for the assistant.
modelSettings.modelHintCustom: Copy the exact model ID from your server.
modelSettings.saveFirst: Save the custom endpoint before testing it.

decisionSettings.saveFailed: Could not save the decision model. Try again.
decisionSettings.testError: Could not test the connection. Try again.
decisionSettings.title: Decision model
decisionSettings.description: Choose a decision provider to filter job requirements, match profile facts, enrich imported jobs, and check claims in drafts.
decisionSettings.cloudflareHint: Create a Workers AI API token for this account in the Cloudflare dashboard.
decisionSettings.modelHint: Use jev-latest or enter a specific version.
decisionSettings.keepKey: Leave blank to keep the current key
decisionSettings.keyHint: Keys are stored encrypted. Without a key, Naruvi uses the language model or built-in rules.

dictationSettings.title: Dictation
dictationSettings.description: How your voice becomes text when you press Dictate. The choice is saved for this browser.

whisper.title: On this computer
whisper.body: Whisper runs in your browser. Your audio never leaves your computer.

cloud.title: Speech API
cloud.body: Google, OpenAI, Groq or Deepgram with your own key. Most accurate; the clip goes to that provider.

browser.title: Browser
browser.body: Words appear as you speak. Chrome sends audio to Google, Edge to Microsoft. Not in Firefox.

dictationSettings.daryCloud: Google understands Moroccan Arabic (ar-MA); the others use Arabic.
dictationSettings.daryWhisper: Whisper uses Arabic for Darija. A Darija-tuned model does better.
dictationSettings.pickHint: Picking it is more accurate than detecting, especially for short clips.

tiny.label: Fast
tiny.note: Quick on any laptop. Good for clear speech.

base.label: Accurate
base.note: Better with accents and noise. A bit slower.

small.label: Best
small.note: Clearly better for French, Arabic and mixed speech. Needs a recent laptop.

custom.label: Your own
custom.note: Any speech model with transformers.js files.

dictationSettings.readyBody: Dictation now runs on this computer.
dictationSettings.customFailedBody: Use a speech-recognition model with ONNX files for transformers.js (e.g. from onnx-community).
dictationSettings.downloadFailedBody: Check your connection and try again.
dictationSettings.idHint: Use the ID as on Hugging Face, like onnx-community/whisper-large-v3-turbo.
dictationSettings.find: Find models that run in the browser:
dictationSettings.optional: Optional. Otherwise it downloads the first time you dictate, then stays cached.
dictationSettings.cloudSavedBody: Test it, or just press Dictate.
dictationSettings.cloudNeedsKey: Add an API key to use it.

notes.google: Strong for French and Moroccan Arabic (ar-MA). Enable the Speech-to-Text API on your key.
notes.groq: Whisper large, very fast and inexpensive.
notes.deepgram: Fast, good for English and noisy audio.

dictationSettings.keepKey: Saved. Leave blank to keep it
dictationSettings.encrypted: Keys are stored encrypted on this server.
